library(shiny)
library(sfsmisc)

lab <- c(ok     = "No assumptions violated",
         right  = "Right-skewed",
         left   = "Left-skewed",
         heavy  = "Heavy-tailed",
         light  = "Light-tailed",
         hetero = "Non-constant variance",
         curve  = "Non-linearity",
         resid  = "Outlier (large residual)",
         lever  = "High-leverage point",
         both   = "Influential outlier")

w <- c(right = 2, left = 2, heavy = 2, light = 2, hetero = 3, curve = 3, resid = 2, lever = 2, both = 2)
w <- c(ok = sum(w) / 3, w)
lam <- 2

scen <- function(s) {
  set.seed(s)
  sample(names(w), 1, prob = w)
}

N <- 100

dif <- rbind(
  curve  = c(Easy = 1.5, Medium = 0.75, Hard = 0.4, Impossible = 0.15),
  R      = c(16, 5, 2.5, 1.3),
  s      = c(0.5, 0.35, 0.22, 0.08),
  shift  = c(6.5, 4.5, 3.5, 2.5),
  lever  = c(8, 6.5, 5.8, 5.3),
  blever = c(12, 9, 7, 5.5),
  bshift = c(4, 2.5, 2.2, 1.2),
  heavy  = c(1, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3),
  light  = c(NA, 50, 6, 4),
  ushape = c(0.5, NA, NA, NA)
)

expl <- c(
  ok     = "The data were simulated to adhere to the assumptions, so any patterns are due to sampling variation.",
  right  = "The distribution is asymmetric, with a longer right tail. In the QQ-plot the points should bend above the line at both ends.",
  left   = "The distribution is asymmetric, with a longer left tail. In the QQ-plot the points should bend below the line at both ends.",
  heavy  = "The tails of the distribution have more mass than a normal distribution. In the QQ-plot the points should bend below the line on the left and above it on the right.",
  light  = "The tails of the distribution have less mass than a normal distribution. In the QQ-plot the points should bend above the line on the left and below it on the right (an S-shape).",
  hetero = "The spread of the error increases with \\(x\\). An upward trend should be visible in the scale-location plot, and a funnel-shape in the residuals vs fitted plot.",
  curve  = "The true relationship is quadratic. The residuals vs fitted plot should display a U-shape.",
  resid  = "One observation is far from the estimated relationship in terms of \\(y\\), but has low leverage, so it has little influence on the slope.",
  lever  = "One observation has an unusual value of \\(x\\), but lies on the true line. Because it agrees with the other observations, it does not distort the estimates.",
  both   = "One observation has an unusual value of \\(x\\) and also departs from the trend, so it pulls the regression line towards itself. How strongly depends on how far it departs, and on the sample size: in larger samples, a single observation has less influence."
)

skew <- function(z, s) (z + s * (z^2 - 1)) / sqrt(1 + 2 * s^2)

mix <- function(z1, z2, g) z1 * exp(g * z2 - g^2)

gn <- function(z, p) {
  a <- qgamma(2 * pnorm(-abs(z)), 1 / p, lower.tail = FALSE)^(1 / p)
  a / sqrt(gamma(3 / p) / gamma(1 / p))
}

ub <- function(z, a) (2 * qbeta(pnorm(-abs(z)), a, a, lower.tail = FALSE) - 1) * sqrt(2 * a + 1)

bal <- function(e, d) {
  a <- abs(e)
  a * rep(c(d, -d), length.out = length(a))[rank(-a, ties.method = "first")]
}

mu <- function(x, type, lvl) if (type == "curve") x + dif["curve", lvl] * (x - 3)^2 / (4 / 3) else x

sim <- function(n, type, lvl = "Medium") {
  p  <- dif[, lvl]
  R  <- p[["R"]]
  x  <- runif(N, 1, 5)
  e  <- rnorm(N)
  z1 <- rnorm(N)
  z2 <- rnorm(N)
  d  <- sample(c(-1, 1), 1)
  i  <- seq_len(N) == 1
  if (type == "resid") x[1] <- 3 + (x[1] - 3) / 4
  if (type == "lever") x[1] <- p[["lever"]]
  if (type == "both")  x[1] <- p[["blever"]]
  if (type %in% c("resid", "lever", "both")) e[1] <- 0
  y <- switch(type,
              ok     = x + e,
              right  = x + skew(z1, p[["s"]]),
              left   = x - skew(z1, p[["s"]]),
              heavy  = x + bal(mix(z1, z2, p[["heavy"]]), d),
              light  = x + bal(if (is.na(p[["ushape"]])) gn(z1, p[["light"]]) else ub(z1, p[["ushape"]]), d),
              hetero = x + R^((x - 3) / 4) / sqrt((R - 1 / R) / (2 * log(R))) * e,
              curve  = mu(x, type, lvl) + e,
              resid  = x + e + p[["shift"]] * d * i,
              lever  = x + e,
              both   = x + e + p[["bshift"]] * d * i)
  data.frame(x, y)[seq_len(n), ]
}

qq <- function(m, lev = 0.95) {
  r <- sort(rstandard(m))
  n <- length(r)
  z <- qnorm(ppoints(n))
  Q <- quantile(r, c(0.25, 0.75))
  b <- unname(diff(Q) / diff(qnorm(c(0.25, 0.75))))
  a <- unname(Q[1] - b * qnorm(0.25))
  k <- qnorm(1 - (1 - lev) / 2)
  u <- seq(-1.05, 1.05, length.out = 200) * max(z)
  Pu <- pnorm(u)
  se <- b / dnorm(u) * sqrt(Pu * (1 - Pu) / n)
  f <- a + b * u
  plot(z, r, type = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "Std. residuals", #asp = 1,
       axes = FALSE, ylim = range(r) * 1.05)
  title(xlab = "Normal quantiles", line = 2)
  mtext("QQ-plot", 3, 0.25)
  grid(lty = 1, equilogs = FALSE)
  eaxis(1)
  eaxis(2)
  polygon(c(u, rev(u)), c(f - k * se, rev(f + k * se)),
          col = adjustcolor("blue", 0.25), border = NA)
  abline(a, b, col = "blue", lwd = 2)
  points(z, r, pch = 19)
  j <- order(abs(r), decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(min(2, n))]
  text(z[j], r[j], names(r)[j], pos = ifelse(z[j] < 0, 4, 2), cex = 0.8)
}

tst <- c(right = "sw", left = "sw", heavy = "sw", light = "sw", hetero = "bp",
         curve = "curv", resid = "out", lever = "lev", both = "cook")

tl <- c(curv = "curvature test", bp = "Breusch–Pagan test", sw = "Shapiro–Wilk test",
        out = "outlier test", cook = "Cook's distance criterion", lev = "leverage criterion")

out <- function(m) {
  n <- length(residuals(m))
  if (n < 4) return(NA)
  min(1, 2 * n * pt(-max(abs(rstudent(m))), n - 3))
}

tests <- function(d) {
  m <- lm(y ~ x, d)
  n <- nrow(d)
  r <- residuals(m)
  c(curv = if (n > 3) summary(lm(y ~ x + I(x^2), d))$coef[3, 4] else NA,
    bp   = pchisq(n * summary(lm(I(r^2) ~ x, d))$r.squared, 1, lower.tail = FALSE),
    sw   = tryCatch(shapiro.test(rstandard(m))$p.value, error = function(e) NA),
    out  = out(m),
    cook = max(cooks.distance(m), na.rm = TRUE),
    lev  = max(hatvalues(m)))
}

flag <- function(p, n) c(curv = isTRUE(p[["curv"]] < 0.05), bp = isTRUE(p[["bp"]] < 0.05),
                         sw = isTRUE(p[["sw"]] < 0.05), out = isTRUE(p[["out"]] < 0.05),
                         cook = isTRUE(p[["cook"]] > 0.5), lev = isTRUE(p[["lev"]] > 6 / n))

pv <- function(p) if (is.na(p)) "n/a" else if (p < 0.001) "\\(p < 0.001\\)" else sprintf("\\(p = %.3f\\)", p)

val <- function(p, k) switch(k, cook = sprintf("\\(D = %.2f\\)", p[["cook"]]),
                             lev = sprintf("\\(h = %.2f\\)", p[["lev"]]), pv(p[[k]]))

gp <- c(right = "norm", left = "norm", heavy = "norm", light = "norm",
        resid = "unus", lever = "unus", both = "unus")

hard <- function(g, y, f) if (g == "ok") !f[[tst[[y]]]] else
  f[[tst[[g]]]] && (y == "ok" || g == "both" || !f[[tst[[y]]]])

colour <- function(g, y, f) {
  if (g == y) return("blue")
  if (isTRUE(gp[g] == gp[y])) return("partial")
  if (hard(g, y, f)) "orange" else "red"
}

bm <- c(Easy = 15, Medium = 10)

bench <- function(b, t) {
  r <- diff(cumsum(c(rep(FALSE, 20), b)), 20)
  if (any(r >= t)) return(tagList(span(style = "color: #4393c3;", "✓"), " reached"))
  sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * tail(r, 1) / t)
}

dat <- function(m, type, lvl) {
  d <- m$model
  n <- nrow(d)
  j <- seq_len(min(3, n))
  i <- unique(c(order(-abs(residuals(m)))[j], order(-abs(rstandard(m)))[j], order(-cooks.distance(m))[j]))
  par(mar = c(5, 5, 3, 3) + 0.1)
  plot(d$x, d$y, type = "n", bty = "n", axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  u <- par("usr")
  par(family = "serif")
  mtext(expression(bold(y)), 2, 3, col = "grey10", las = 1, cex = par("cex"))
  mtext(expression(bold(x)), 1, 3, col = "grey10", cex = par("cex"))
  par(family = "sans")
  rect(u[1], u[3], u[2], u[4], col = "grey97", border = NA)
  g <- function(t) seq(t[1] - diff(t[1:2]), t[length(t)] + diff(t[1:2]), diff(t[1:2]) / 2)
  abline(h = g(axTicks(2)), v = g(axTicks(1)), lwd = 2, col = "white")
  abline(h = axTicks(2), v = axTicks(1), lwd = 3, col = "white")
  eaxis(1, col = "grey25", col.axis = "grey25", col.ticks = "grey25", small.args = list(col = "grey25"))
  eaxis(2, col = "grey25", col.axis = "grey25", col.ticks = "grey25", small.args = list(col = "grey25"))
  curve(mu(x, type, lvl), u[1], u[2], add = TRUE, col = "grey", lwd = 3)
  abline(coef(m), col = "steelblue", lwd = 3)
  legend("topleft", c("Fitted line", "True relationship"), col = c("steelblue", "grey"), lwd = 3, bty = "n")
  points(d$x, d$y, pch = 19)
  text(d$x[i], d$y[i], rownames(d)[i], pos = ifelse(d$x[i] > mean(u[1:2]), 2, 4), cex = 0.8)
}

diag4 <- function(m) {
  sm <- function(x, y, ...) panel.smooth(x, y, col.smooth = "blue", iter = 3, ...)
  yl <- list("Residuals", NULL, expression(sqrt(abs("Std. residuals"))), NULL,
             "Std. residuals")
  for(i in c(1, 2, 3, 5)){
    if(i == 2){
      qq(m)
      next
    }
    plot(m, which = i, pch = 19, panel = sm, axes = FALSE, ann = FALSE, sub.caption = "")
    title(ylab = yl[[i]])
    if(i == 5){
      axis(4, -5:5, rep("", 11), col = "white", tck = 0, lwd = 3)
      title(xlab = "Leverage", line = 2)
    } else{
      title(xlab = "Fitted values", line = 2)
    }
    eaxis(1)
    eaxis(2)
  }
}

sec <- function(t, ...) tags$details(class = "sec", style = "margin-bottom: 0.75em;",
                                     tags$summary(fontawesome::fa("chevron-right", fill = "steelblue"), " ", strong(t)),
                                     div(style = "margin: 0.5em 0 0 1em;", ...))

css <- "
details.sec > summary { display: list-item; list-style: none; cursor: pointer; font-size: 1.1em;
  padding: 0.4em 0.75em; background-color: #f2f6fa; border: 1px solid #d6e0ea; border-radius: 4px; }
details.sec > summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; }
details.sec > summary:hover { background-color: #e4edf5; }
details.sec > summary svg { transition: transform 0.15s; }
details.sec[open] > summary svg { transform: rotate(90deg); }
details.sec > summary::after { content: 'show'; float: right; color: grey; font-size: 85%; }
details.sec[open] > summary::after { content: 'hide'; }
.phone-only { display: none; }
@media (max-width: 599px) { .phone-only { display: inline-block; } .btn { padding: 3px 10px; } .form-group { margin-bottom: 5px; } }
#guess.locked { opacity: 0.6; }
#guess.locked label { cursor: default; }
#guess.locked input:checked + span { font-weight: bold; }
.alert.fb-blue { background-color: #92c5de; border-color: #4393c3; color: #000; }
.alert.fb-orange { background-color: #fde0a6; border-color: #f4a442; color: #000; }
.alert.fb-red { background-color: #efa7a7; border-color: #d6604d; color: #000; }
.alert.fb-partial { background-color: #d1e5f0; border-color: #92c5de; color: #000; }
details.ans > summary { display: list-item; cursor: pointer; color: grey; font-size: 85%; }
"

js <- "
Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('lock', function(x) {
  $('#guess').toggleClass('locked', x);
  $('input[name=guess], #check').prop('disabled', x);
  $('input[name=view]').prop('disabled', !x);
});
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
  var tex = function(el) {
    renderMathInElement(el, {delimiters: [{left: '\\\\(', right: '\\\\)', display: false},
                                          {left: '\\\\[', right: '\\\\]', display: true}], throwOnError: false});
  };
  tex(document.body);
  new MutationObserver(function(ms) {
    ms.forEach(function(m) { if (m.addedNodes.length) tex(m.target); });
  }).observe(document.body, {childList: true, subtree: true});
});
"

kx <- "https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/KaTeX/0.16.11/"

item <- function(t, ...) tagList(tags$dt(t), tags$dd(style = "margin-bottom: 0.6em;", ...))

sh <- c(ok = "No assumptions violated", right = "Right-skewed", left = "Left-skewed", heavy = "Heavy tailed",
        light = "Light tailed", curve = "Non-linearity", hetero = "Non-constant variance",
        resid = "Large residual", lever = "High leverage", both = "Both")

grp <- list(" " = list("ok"), "Deviations from normality:" = list(c("left", "right"), c("heavy", "light")),
            "Mean and variance:" = list(c("curve", "hetero")),
            "Unusual observation:" = list(c("resid", "lever", "both")))

opt <- function(k, first) tags$label(class = "radio-inline",
                                     style = paste0("margin: 0 0 0.25em 0;",
                                                    if (k == "ok") " grid-column: 1 / -1;" else if (first) " grid-column: 1;"),
                                     tags$input(type = "radio", name = "guess", value = k), span(sh[[k]]))

row <- function(k) lapply(seq_along(k), function(i) opt(k[i], i == 1))

guess <- div(id = "guess", class = "form-group shiny-input-radiogroup shiny-input-container", role = "radiogroup",
             `aria-labelledby` = "guess-label", style = "width: auto;",
             tags$label(class = "control-label", id = "guess-label", `for` = "guess", style = "margin-bottom: 0.6em;",
                        "What are you looking at?"),
             div(class = "shiny-options-group",
                 style = "display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, max-content)); column-gap: 1em;",
                 lapply(names(grp), function(g) tagList(
                   if (g != " ") div(style = "grid-column: 1 / -1; margin-top: 0.3em; font-size: 85%; color: grey;", g),
                   lapply(grp[[g]], row)))))

ref <- tagList(
  tags$head(tags$style(HTML(css))),
  hr(),
  h3(id = "explanation", "Explanation"),
  p("The sections on statistical terminology and diagnostic plots cover what you should know for this course. ",
    "The section on significance tests goes into more detail than you need, and is merely there for reference."),
  sec("Statistical terminology", tags$dl(
    item("Fitted value",
         "The value of the outcome predicted by the model for an observation: ",
         "\\(\\hat{y}_i = \\hat{\\beta}_0 + \\hat{\\beta}_1 x_i\\)."),
    item("Residual",
         "The difference between an observed and a fitted value: \\(\\hat{\\epsilon}_i = y_i - \\hat{y}_i\\)."),
    item("Standardized residual",
         "A residual divided by its estimated standard deviation. If the assumptions hold, standardized ",
         "residuals are approximately normally distributed with a standard deviation of \\(1\\), so values beyond \\(\\pm 2\\) occur about 5% of the ",
         "time, and values beyond \\(\\pm 3\\) about 0.3%. In a sample of 100, you therefore expect about five ",
         "residuals beyond \\(\\pm 2\\) even when every assumption holds.",
         " See: ", a(href = "https://fransrodenburg.github.io/Applied-Statistics/normaldistribution.html",
                    target = "_blank", rel = "noopener noreferrer",
                    fontawesome::fa("dice-one", fill = "steelblue", title = "A six-sided die"),
                    " Normal Distribution"), "."),
    item("Leverage",
         "How far an observation's value of \\(x\\) lies from the mean of \\(x\\). It measures the ",
         "observation's potential to pull the regression line towards itself, and does not depend on ",
         "\\(y\\). In simple linear regression, the average leverage is \\(2/n\\)."),
    item("Outlier",
         "An observation that lies far from the regression line, that is, with a large residual."),
    item("Influential observation",
         "An observation whose removal would change the estimates substantially. Influence requires both ",
         "high leverage and a large residual: A point far out on \\(x\\) that follows the trend has high ",
         "leverage, but usually little influence."),
    item("Cook's distance",
         "A measure of influence: How much the fitted values would change if the observation were left out."),
    item("Smoother",
         "The blue curve in the residuals vs fitted and scale-location plots: A ",
         "local average that shows the trend in the points. It is unstable in ",
         "small samples, as well as near the edges of the plot in general."),
    item("Sampling variation",
         "Differences between samples from the same population that arise by chance alone. It is why ",
         "plots of data that meet every assumption can still show apparent patterns."),
    item("Seed",
         "A number that fixes the random number generator, so that the same sample can be generated again.")
  )),
  sec("Diagnostic plots", tags$dl(
    item("Residuals vs fitted",
         "The distance from the regression line plotted against the height of the regression line. If the assumptions hold, the points scatter randomly ",
         "around zero, without a pattern. A curved pattern (for example a U-shape) indicates non-linearity, ",
         "a funnel shape can indicate non-constant variance, and isolated points far from zero suggest outliers."),
    item("QQ-plot",
         "The standardized residuals against the quantiles expected under a normal distribution. ",
         "If the error were truly normal, the points follow the straight line. The shaded band is a pointwise 95% ",
         "band: It applies to each point separately, so in larger samples a few points outside it are ",
         "expected even under normality. Skewness bends both ends in the same direction (upwards for right ",
         "skew, downwards for left skew). Heavy tails result in points below the line on the ",
         "left and above it on the right; light tails give the reverse (an S-shape)."),
    item("Scale-location",
         "The transformation \\(\\sqrt{|\\text{std. res.}|}\\) makes it easier to assess non-constant variance, ",
         "because up = greater variance and down = lower variance. If the ",
         "variance is constant, the smoother is roughly flat. An upward or downward trend indicates that ",
         "the spread of the error changes with the fitted values."),
    item("Residuals vs leverage",
         "The standardized residuals against the leverage, with dashed contours of Cook's distance at 0.5 ",
         "and 1. Points far to the right have high leverage, points far up or down have large residuals, ",
         "and points beyond the contours are influential.")
  )),
  sec("Difficulty levels",
      p("The difficulty sets the size of the deviation in new samples. The same seed gives the same random ",
        "noise at every level, so you can compare how a deviation looks at different difficulties. To do so, ",
        "enter the seed of the example, change the difficulty and press 'New sample'."),
      tags$dl(
        item("Easy",
             "Large deviations. Learn the typical pattern of each deviation and the plot in which it shows. ",
             "At \\(n = 30\\), you should be able to score 75% or more correct."),
        item("Medium",
             "Clear deviations, closer to what you may encounter in actual data. Recognize problems that ",
             "clearly matter. At \\(n = 30\\), you should be able to score 50% or more correct."),
        item("Hard",
             "Small deviations, not necessarily large enough to be a problem. At \\(n = 30\\), any score ",
             "clearly above 25% is good."),
        item("Impossible",
             "Subtle deviations, about as large as sampling variation. In small samples, they are practically ",
             "impossible to detect, by eye or by any test.")
      )),
  sec("Significance tests",
      p("After each answer, the app shows the results of four significance tests (flagged when ",
        "\\(p < 0.05\\)) and two rules of thumb on the same sample, so that you can compare your own judgment ",
        "with what a test would have concluded. A significance test asks whether a deviation can be detected ",
        "in this sample, not whether it is large enough to matter, so its result depends strongly on sample size."),
      tags$dl(
        item("Curvature test",
             "Adds \\(x^2\\) to the model and tests whether its coefficient differs from zero. Detects ",
             "curvature that is roughly quadratic (a U-shape or its reverse), but is less sensitive to other ",
             "forms of non-linearity. The test itself assumes normal errors with constant variance. Requires ",
             "\\(n \\geq 4\\)."),
        item("Breusch\u2013Pagan test",
             "Regresses the squared residuals on \\(x\\) and tests whether they increase or decrease with ",
             "\\(x\\). Detects variance that changes steadily with \\(x\\), but can miss variance that is, for ",
             "example, larger in the middle than at the edges. Outliers and non-linearity can also make it ",
             "significant. The version used here (Koenker's) does not require normal errors."),
        item("Shapiro\u2013Wilk test",
             "Tests whether the standardized residuals are consistent with a normal distribution, essentially ",
             "by measuring how closely they follow the straight line in the QQ-plot. It is particularly good at ",
             "detecting skewness, but weaker against symmetric deviations, especially light tails."),
        item("Outlier test (Bonferroni)",
             "Takes the largest absolute studentized residual and assesses how unusual it is, correcting for ",
             "the fact that it is the largest of \\(n\\). Detects a single outlier; several outliers can mask ",
             "each other, and the correction makes the test conservative. Requires \\(n \\geq 4\\)."),
        item("Cook's distance (maximum)",
             "Not a significance test, but a conventional rule of thumb: values above 0.5 are labelled ",
             "possibly influential, and above 1 influential. In small samples, it is often exceeded even when ",
             "every assumption holds: at \\(n = 10\\), the largest Cook's distance exceeds 0.5 in about half of ",
             "such samples in this app. A high-leverage point that follows the trend usually stays below 0.5, ",
             "but with very high leverage, even a small residual can push it above."),
        item("Leverage (maximum)",
             "Not a significance test, but a conventional rule of thumb: Flagged when the largest leverage exceeds three times the ",
             "average, \\(6/n\\). It depends only on \\(x\\), so it identifies points with the potential to be ",
             "influential, not necessarily points that are outlying.")
      ))
)

ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$head(tags$link(rel = "stylesheet", href = paste0(kx, "katex.min.css")),
            tags$script(src = paste0(kx, "katex.min.js"), defer = NA),
            tags$script(src = paste0(kx, "contrib/auto-render.min.js"), defer = NA),
            tags$script(HTML(js))),
  style = "max-width: 1000px; margin: auto;",
  titlePanel(tagList("Interactive App — Model Diagnostics"),
             windowTitle = "Interactive App — Model Diagnostics"),
  p("Each time you press 'New sample', a data set is simulated, a simple linear model ",
    "is fitted, and its diagnostic plots are shown. ",
    sprintf("About %.0f%% of the samples meet every assumption; ", 100 * w[["ok"]] / sum(w)),
    "the rest contain one deliberate deviation. Decide what you are looking at, then check your answer. Afterwards, you can switch to 'Resulting model' to see the data and the true relationship. Once you have a feel for it, try the exercises below."),
  tags$details(id = "note", class = "sec", style = "margin-bottom: 0.75em;",
               tags$summary(fontawesome::fa("chevron-right", fill = "steelblue"), " ", strong("Note")),
    div(class = "small", style = "margin-top: 0.75em;",
        tags$ol(
          tags$li("The QQ-plot can reveal specific deviations from normality, as covered in the ",
                  a(href = "https://youtu.be/_B6VDSa9N60?t=317", target = "_blank", rel = "noopener noreferrer",
                    fontawesome::fa("youtube", fill = "red"), " video ",
                    fontawesome::fa("arrow-up-right-from-square", height = "0.75em"),
                    .noWS = c("after", "before-end")), "."),
          tags$li("This is an exercise in diagnostic plots of ordinary linear models only. In an actual analysis:",
                  tags$ol(type = "a",
                          tags$li("the choice of model follows from the type of outcome and the study design ",
                                  em("first", .noWS = "after"), ". Diagnostic plots come ", em("second", .noWS = "after"),
                                  ", once the model has been justified from theory;"),
                          tags$li("the assumptions should not be checked with a battery of significance tests. ",
                                  "Testing assumptions this way has inherent problems, as this exercise shows."))),
          tags$li("Not familiar with a term or test? See the ", a(href = "#explanation", "explanation section"),
                  " at the bottom of the page. You can do the exercise without fully understanding every term or test.")))),
  hr(),
  fluidRow(
    column(3, sliderInput("n", "Sample size", min = 3, max = 100, value = 30)),
    column(2, selectInput("lvl", "Difficulty", colnames(dif), "Easy")),
    column(3, textInput("seed", tagList(strong("Seed"),
                                        span(style = "color: grey; font-weight: normal;", "(blank = random)")), "")),
    column(4, div(style = "font-size: 85%; line-height: 20px;", textOutput("pos", inline = TRUE)),
           actionButton("new", "New sample"),
           actionButton("prev", "Previous", style = "color: #888; border-color: #ddd;"),
           actionButton("nxt", "Next", style = "color: #888; border-color: #ddd;"), br(),
           div(style = "font-size: 85%;", uiOutput("used")))
  ),
  radioButtons("view", NULL, c("Diagnostic plots" = "diag", "Resulting model" = "data"), inline = TRUE),
  imageOutput("diag", height = "auto"),
  div(style = "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; column-gap: 2em;",
      div(style = "flex: 0 0 auto;", guess),
      div(style = "flex: 1 1 18em; min-width: 0;",
          actionButton("check", "Check answer"),
          tags$button(type = "button", class = "btn btn-default phone-only",
                      onclick = "document.getElementById('new').click(); document.getElementById('used').scrollIntoView();",
                      "New sample"), br(),
          uiOutput("fb"))),
  uiOutput("score"),
  hr(),
  h3("Exercise"),
  p("You have done enough once you can answer these two questions."),
  tags$ol(
    tags$li("Reach the benchmark at Easy, then at Medium (shown in the results table). Which plot gave away which deviation?",
            tags$details(class = "ans", tags$summary("Answer"),
                         p("The four deviations from normality show in the QQ-plot. Non-linearity shows as a curve in ",
                           "the residuals vs fitted plot. Non-constant variance shows as a trend in the scale-location ",
                           "plot, and as a funnel in the residuals vs fitted plot. Unusual observations stand out in the ",
                           "residuals vs leverage plot: far to the right (high leverage), far up or down (large residual), ",
                           "or both."))),
    tags$li("Play a few rounds at \\(n = 10\\), and compare your answers with the test results. Then generate one of ",
            "those samples again at \\(n = 100\\) with the same seed. What does this tell you about checking ",
            "assumptions in small studies?",
            tags$details(class = "ans", tags$summary("Answer"),
                         p("At \\(n = 10\\), the plots and the tests are both unreliable: the checks often flag a ",
                           "problem in data that meet every assumption, and real deviations are easily missed. With ",
                           "more data, the same sample shows the deviation, or its absence, much more clearly. A small ",
                           "study can neither confirm nor rule out a violation; the assumptions then have to be ",
                           "justified by the study design and prior knowledge.")))
  ),
  ref
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  H     <- reactiveVal(list())
  pos   <- reactiveVal(0)
  pend  <- reactiveVal(NULL)

  cur    <- reactive(H()[[req(pos())]])
  latest <- reactive(pos() == length(H()))
  lk     <- reactive(!latest() || !is.null(cur()$ans))

  observe({
    req(length(H()) > 0)
    a <- cur()$ans
    s <- if (!is.null(a)) a else if (!lk()) isolate(pend())
    updateRadioButtons(session, "guess", selected = if (is.null(s)) character(0) else s)
    if (!lk()) updateRadioButtons(session, "view", selected = "diag")
    session$sendCustomMessage("lock", lk())
  })
  # 
  observeEvent(input$guess, if (latest() && is.null(cur()$ans)) pend(input$guess))
  
  observeEvent(input$new, {
    s <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(input$seed))
    if (is.na(s)) {
      O <- c(table(factor(vapply(H(), `[[`, "", "type"), names(w))))
      y <- sample(names(w), 1, prob = w * exp(lam * pmax(0, length(H()) * w / sum(w) - O)))
      S <- sample.int(1e6, 1000)
      s <- c(Find(function(s) scen(s) == y, S), S[1])[1]
    }
    type <- scen(s)
    d <- sim(input$n, type, input$lvl)
    e <- list(seed = s, n = input$n, lvl = input$lvl, type = type, d = d, p = tests(d), ans = NULL)
    pend(NULL)
    H(c(H(), list(e)))
    pos(length(H()))
    updateTextInput(session, "seed", value = "")
  }, ignoreNULL = FALSE)

  observeEvent(input$prev, pos(max(1, pos() - 1)))
  observeEvent(input$nxt, pos(min(length(H()), pos() + 1)))

  observeEvent(input$check, {
    req(latest(), input$guess, is.null(cur()$ans))
    h <- H()
    h[[pos()]]$ans <- input$guess
    H(h)
  })

  output$pos  <- renderText(sprintf("Example %d of %d", req(pos()), length(H())))
  output$used <- renderUI(tagList(sprintf("%s difficulty, \\(n = %d\\), seed:", cur()$lvl, cur()$n),
                                  span(style = "font-family: monospace;", cur()$seed)))
  
  output$diag <- renderImage({
    m <- lm(y ~ x, cur()$d)
    wd <- req(session$clientData$output_diag_width)
    nar <- wd < 600
    dv <- lk() && identical(input$view, "data")
    h <- round(wd * if (dv && nar) 1 else if (nar) 3 else 9/16)
    f <- tempfile(fileext = ".svg")
    svg(f, width = wd / 96, height = h / 96)
    par(mfrow = if (dv) c(1, 1) else if (nar) c(4, 1) else c(2, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 2) + 0.1, mgp = c(2.75, 0.75, 0))
    par(cex = 0.83)
    if (dv) dat(m, cur()$type, cur()$lvl) else diag4(m)
    dev.off()
    list(src = f, width = wd, height = h, contentType = "image/svg+xml")
  }, deleteFile = TRUE)
  
  output$fb <- renderUI({
    g <- cur()$ans
    if (is.null(g)) return(if (!latest()) div(class = "alert alert-secondary", "Not answered."))
    y <- cur()$type
    p <- cur()$p
    n <- cur()$n
    f <- flag(p, n)
    k <- colour(g, y, f)
    cd <- if (p[["cook"]] > 1) " (influential)" else if (p[["cook"]] > 0.5) " (possibly influential)" else ""
    hl <- if (p[["lev"]] > 6 / n) " (high)" else ""
    div(class = paste0("alert fb-", k),
                    strong(switch(k, blue = "Correct. ", partial = "Close. ", "Not quite. ")),
                    paste0("This was: ", lab[y], ". ", expl[y]),
                    if (y == "light" && cur()$lvl == "Easy")
                      paste(" At this difficulty, the error distribution has two peaks, one at each end of its range.",
                            "In actual data, this can indicate a missing grouping variable, for example two groups",
                            "with different means that the model treats as one."),
                    if (k == "partial") if (gp[[y]] == "norm")
                      " You identified the right assumption (normality), but not the pattern." else
                      " You identified the unusual observation, but not its type.",
                    if (g != y && hard(g, y, f)) {
                      if (g == "ok") paste0(" This was a hard example: the ", tl[[tst[[y]]]], " would not have flagged it either (",
                                            val(p, tst[[y]]), ").")
                      else if (y == "ok") paste0(" This was a hard example: the ", tl[[tst[[g]]]], " also flagged this sample (",
                                                 val(p, tst[[g]]), "), although every assumption held.")
                      else paste0(" This was a hard example: the ", tl[[tst[[g]]]], " also flagged this sample (",
                                  val(p, tst[[g]]), ")",
                                  if (!f[[tst[[y]]]]) paste0(", but the ", tl[[tst[[y]]]], " did not (", val(p, tst[[y]]), ")"), ".")
                    },
                    if (cur()$lvl == "Impossible" && y != "ok")
                      " At this level, the deviation is about as visible as sampling noise. Try the same seed at Easy to see it clearly.",
                    br(), br(),
                    em(style = "font-size: 85%;", sprintf(paste0("Curvature test %s, Breusch–Pagan %s, Shapiro–Wilk %s, ",
                                                                 "outlier test %s, max. Cook's distance %s%s, max. leverage %s%s."),
                                                          pv(p[["curv"]]), pv(p[["bp"]]), pv(p[["sw"]]), pv(p[["out"]]),
                                                          val(p, "cook"), cd, val(p, "lev"), hl)))
  })
  
  output$score <- renderUI({
    h <- Filter(function(e) !is.null(e$ans), H())
    k <- vapply(h, function(e) colour(e$ans, e$type, flag(e$p, e$n)), "")
    L <- vapply(h, `[[`, "", "lvl")
    Y <- vapply(h, `[[`, "", "type")
    dv <- setdiff(unlist(grp), "ok")
    ok <- dv %in% Y[k == "blue"]
    td <- function(...) tags$td(..., style = "text-align: center;")
    th <- function(...) tags$th(..., style = "text-align: center;")
    l <- intersect(colnames(dif), L)
    rows <- if (!length(l)) tags$tr(tags$td(colspan = 5, style = "color: grey;", "No answers yet")) else
      lapply(l, function(l) {
        i <- L == l
        tags$tr(tags$td(if (l == "Impossible") em(l) else l),
                td(sprintf("%d of %d (%.0f%%)", sum(k[i] == "blue"), sum(i), 100 * mean(k[i] == "blue"))),
                td(sum(k[i] == "partial")),
                td(sum(k[i] == "orange")),
                td(if (l %in% names(bm)) bench(k[i] == "blue", bm[[l]]) else "–"))
      })
    tagList(
      h4("Results"),
      div(style = "overflow-x: auto;", tags$table(class = "table table-condensed",
                                                  tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th("Difficulty"), th("Correct"),
                                                                     th("Close"), th("Hard (orange)"),
                                                                     th("Benchmark"))),
                                                  tags$tbody(rows))),
      p(style = "margin-bottom: 0.25em;", sprintf("Deviations identified (%d of %d):", sum(ok), length(dv))),
      div(id = "dev", style = "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; column-gap: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em;",
          lapply(seq_along(dv), function(j) if (ok[j]) span(span(style = "color: #4393c3;", "✓"), " ", sh[[dv[j]]]) else
            span(style = "color: grey;", sh[[dv[j]]]))),
      p(style = "font-size: 85%; color: grey;",
        "Close: the right assumption, or the unusual observation, but the wrong pattern or type.", br(),
        "Hard (orange): wrong answers for which the checks pointed to your answer rather than to the correct one.", br(),
        sprintf("Always answering '%s' would give about %.0f%% correct at any level.",
                lab["ok"], 100 * w[["ok"]] / sum(w))))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
